POWERING INDIA’S  
FUTURE WITH  
CLEAN NUCLEAR ENERGY
Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi laid the Foundation Stone for ASHVINI’s 
Mahi Banswara Rajasthan Atomic Power Project - MBRAPP (4X700 MW) at Banswara on the 25 September 2025. Located in Banswara district of Rajasthan, the project entails an investment of around Rs 42,000 crore. Upon completion, this project will be one of the largest nuclear plants in the country supplying reliable base load energy and will strengthen India’s position in the environmental stewardship & evolving nuclear energy landscape.
MBRAPP is being developed by Anushakti Vidhyut Nigam Ltd (ASHVINI)— with joint 
participation of NPCIL (51%) and NTPC (49%) pooling the financial, technological, and project expertise of both companies.
MBRAPP will comprise of four indigenous 700 MW Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors 
(PHWRs) with advanced safety features - also known as IPHWR 700 - designed and developed by NPCIL. The project is part of India’s broader “fleet mode” initiative, where ten identical 700 MW reactors are being built across India under uniform design and procurement plans. Three such reactors have been commissioned, and Mahi Banswara is also part of the fleet. This approach promotes the spirit of Atmanirbhar Bharat and brings in cost efficiencies, faster deployment, and consolidated operational expertise.
MBRAPP will supply clean, affordable and reliable power to Rajasthan and other 
beneficiaries. This will create direct & indirect employment opportunities and will support local communities, businesses, and industries, supporting the economic growth and prosperity in the state and the country.

About the Report
We are pleased to present our Annual Report of NTPC Limited for the financial year ended March 31, 2026. The 
Annual Report presents a cohesive narrative that connects NTPC's financial strength, operational achievements, 
and the broader impact it creates, linking performance metrics with the strategic thinking that drives them. 
Beyond fulfilling compliance requirements, it provides stakeholders with meaningful insights into how NTPC manages complexity, allocates resources, and makes strategic decisions that shape long-term value.
This Report has been prepared in accordance with the principles and 
content elements of the International <IR> Framework, developed 
by the International Integrated Reporting Council (IIRC)  and now 
under the purview of the IFRS Foundation  through the International 
Sustainability Standards Boards (ISSB).   
The report draws from globally and nationally accepted frameworks 
to guide its structure and disclosures, including the Business 
Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR)  framework 
based on the National Guidelines for Responsible Business Conduct 
(NGRBC), requirements of key indicators of Global Reporting 
Initiative (GRI) Standards 2021,  and the United Nations Sustainable 
Development Goals (UN SDGs) and the United Nations Global 
Compact (UNGC) principles.
In addition, we adhere to applicable regulatory requirements such 
as the Companies Act, 2013, Indian Accounting Standards (Ind 
AS), and SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015, along with the Secretarial Standards issued by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI).
The report captures information on the financial and non-financial 
performance for the period April 1, 2025, to March 31, 2026. The Financial disclosure scope of boundary includes all our operations 
and business activities within the NTPC Group, covering NTPC 
Limited, our subsidiaries, and our joint ventures.
For the non-financial performance disclosure, the scope of boundary 
restricts NTPC Limited and those subsidiaries, and joint ventures, on which NTPC has operational and financial control.The financial statements, both standalone and consolidated, have 
been audited by the Statutory Auditors. Business Responsibility and 
Sustainability Report, Core Indicators have been assured by a third-party, TUV India Private Limited, based on ISAE 3000 Standards 
for FY 2025-26.  
This report contains statements that relate to future events and 
expectations. Words such as "expects," "intends," "believes," "plans," 
"estimates," "may," "will," "should," or similar terms indicate forward-
looking statements. These are grounded in current assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties outside NTPC's control. Actual 
results may differ materially from what has been stated or implied.

Energising India’s Growth, 
Powering the Transition
Aligning NTPC’s growth with India’s vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 and Net Zero @2070
India has set itself two defining goals for the decades ahead: to become a developed nation Viksit Bharat by 2047, the centenary of its 
independence, and to achieve Net Zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2070. For NTPC, India’s largest integrated power utility, supporting 
both goals lies at the heart of our purpose and our long-term strategy.
The world's energy system is undergoing a rapid transformation 
as governments and businesses accelerate their decarbonisation 
efforts. According to Net Zero Tracker, 137 countries have already established net-zero targets, while 145 countries have 
announced or are considering net-zero commitments. Reflecting 
this global shift, the International Energy Agency (IEA) reports that clean energy is attracting an increasingly larger share of 
new investment in power generation worldwide.Solar, wind 
and battery storage are being added to record levels each year, supported by a sustained fall in technology costs over the past 
decade. At the same time, governments are placing renewed 
emphasis on energy security, resilient supply chains for critical minerals, and the need to keep energy affordable through a 
period of global uncertainty.
India approaches this transition as one of the world’s fastest-
growing major economies and its most populous nation, even as 
its per-capita energy use and emissions remain well below the global average. India’s transition is therefore distinctive: it must 
serve a large and rising demand for energy while steadily reducing 
the carbon intensity of that energy. This approach is guided by the principles of equity and common but differentiated responsibilities, 
as reflected in India’s commitments under the UNFCCC and its 
Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy.The Global Energy TransitionNITI Aayog’s study, Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat and Net Zero, provides a comprehensive assessment of how India can pursue 
rapid development and deep decarbonization together. As per its 
scenarios, India’s economy is projected to grow from around USD 4.2 trillion in 2025 to about USD 30 trillion by 2047, accompanied by 
rapid urbanization and a multi-fold increase in the output of steel, 
cement and other materials as the country moves closer to global per-capita consumption levels.
A notable feature of these scenarios is that energy demand 
grows far more slowly than the economy. Final energy demand is 
projected to rise only about 2.1 to 2.6 times by 2070, even as GDP 
expands roughly elevenfold, on account of greater electrification, improved energy efficiency and circularity. Electricity is at the centre 
of this shift. Its share of final energy consumption is projected to 
rise from around 21% at present to as much as 60% by 2070, while total electricity demand could grow six to eight times over the 
same period, lifting per-capita consumption towards the levels of advanced economies. The pace at which the power grid becomes 
cleaner will, in large measure, determine the pace of decarbonization 
across the wider economy.
Meeting India’s electricity needs cleanly calls for a transformation of unprecedented scale. NITI Aayog’s Net Zero Scenario indicates 
that total installed generation capacity could grow roughly fourteen times by 2070, with renewable energy forming the new core of 
the grid. Solar becomes the backbone, with capacity potentially 
exceeding 5,000 GW, complemented by more than 1,000 GW of wind, including offshore wind off the coasts of Gujarat and Tamil 
Nadu. The share of non-fossil capacity rises from around 40% at 
present to close to 98% by 2070.India’s Twin Goals: Viksit Bharat and Net Zero
Transforming the Power Sector
As variable renewables come to dominate, energy storage and 
firm power become essential to maintaining reliability. In the 
same scenarios, battery energy storage is projected to scale from 
negligible levels today to 2,500–3,000 GW by 2070, supported 
by 150–165 GW of pumped hydro. Nuclear power emerges as a strategic pillar of firm, low-carbon generation, scaling from 
around 8 GW today (Central Electricity Authority) towards 100 GW 
by 2047, in line with the national nuclear mission, and potentially 300 GW by 2070 in NITI Aayog’s projections, with small modular 
reactors playing an increasing role.
Coal continues to play a vital role through the transition. In the near-
to-medium term, the existing coal fleet remains important for grid 
reliability and for meeting demand during periods of high system stress. In these scenarios, coal capacity is expected to peak 
around the mid-2040s before declining as long-duration storage 
and clean alternatives mature. The emphasis, therefore, is on improving the efficiency, flexibility and environmental performance 
of the coal fleet so that it can support a renewable-rich grid, while 
avoiding long-term lock-ins. This balanced approach, which secures reliability even as the system decarbonises, is precisely 
where a utility of NTPC’s scale and operating experience adds the 
greatest value.

For sectors that are difficult to electrify directly, such as heavy 
industry and long-distance transport, green hydrogen emerges 
as a key clean-energy carrier. It can serve as a reducing agent in 
green steelmaking, a feedstock for green ammonia and fertilisers, 
a cleaner input for refineries, and the basis for green methanol and ammonia in shipping. Under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, India aims to produce 5 million tonnes of green hydrogen each year by 2030, while NITI Aayog’s Net Zero Scenario projects demand rising towards 25 million tonnes by 2050 and around 50 
million tonnes by 2070. Because most green hydrogen is produced 
through renewable-powered electrolysis, its growth is closely linked to the expansion of clean power.
The transition is capital-intensive. NITI Aayog estimates cumulative investment of around USD 22.7 trillion by 2070 under the Net Zero 
Scenario, with the power sector accounting for over half of the total, 
reflecting its central role in electrifying the wider economy. This implies average annual flows of close to USD 500 billion, against 
actual energy investment of about USD 135 billion in 2024 (IEA). 
Mobilising capital on this scale, attracting low-cost finance, and building domestic manufacturing and innovation capacity are 
among the defining tasks of the coming decades.
The human dimension of the transition is equally important. NITI 
Aayog’s assessment of the social implications of the transition notes that more than 150 districts depend significantly on fossil-
fuel supply chains, and that coal-based power and mining together 
sustain millions of formal and informal livelihoods. Encouragingly, 
the same analysis finds that the Net Zero pathway is expected to create more energy-sector jobs than it displaces, with around 
one million additional energy jobs by 2050, alongside substantial 
gains in construction and clean-technology manufacturing, provided the transition is managed with care through reskilling, 
livelihood diversification and support for affected communities. 
NTPC remains committed to a just energy transition, ensuring that progress towards a cleaner energy system continues to create 
opportunity and shared prosperity.
As the nation’s largest power producer, NTPC has a central role to play in this transformation. With an installed and commercial 
group capacity of over 90 GW, NTPC meets close to one-fourth of India’s electricity requirement. The Company has built its standing 
on reliability, operational excellence and affordable power, and is 
now applying the same discipline to one of the most ambitious diversification journeys in the global power sector. In line with our 
vision to be the world’s leading power company, accelerating India’s 
growth along with energy transition, the company is strengthening its existing core business while building a new core in renewables, 
storage, nuclear, green hydrogen and green chemicals.
At the centre of this strategy is The Brighter Plan, NTPC’s roadmap 
to reshape its portfolio around clean energy to address the triple 
bottom line. The Company has set a target of 60 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2032, as part of a planned total capacity of around 149 GW, with non-fossil sources expected to constitute 
nearly half of the portfolio. This is envisaged to scale up to 244 GW 
by 2037, out of which 136 GW will come from RE portfolio, and the non-fossil fuel based capacity will gain 60% of the capacity share. 
To drive this growth, NTPC has carved out and listed NTPC Green 
Energy Limited (NGEL),  its dedicated renewable energy arm, which 
has crossed 10 GW of installed capacity and is developing gigawatt-scale solar, wind and hybrid parks, including the flagship Khavda 
complex in Gujarat, under the Ultra Mega Renewable Energy Power Park model. To champion the other part of the clean energy portfolio 
by addition of Nuclear Energy, the company is already in process 
to setup its first nuclear power project in Banswara, Rajasthan under its joint venture with Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd 
(NPCIL), while setting up another wholly owned subsidiary NTPC 
Parmanu Urja Nigam Limited (NPUNL) to add nuclear capacities across India.Green Hydrogen and the Hard-to-Abate Sectors
Financing the Transition and a Just Energy Transition
NTPC: Powering India’s Energy TransitionA rapidly expanding solar, wind, floating-solar and hybrid 
portfolio, backed by battery storage and pumped-hydro 
projects to firm up variable generation and to provide grid 
balancing and ancillary services.
Pilot and demonstration projects in green hydrogen mobility 
and microgrids, setting up India’s first and largest Green Hydrogen Hub at Pudimadaka, Vishakhapatnam, hydrogen 
blending in natural-gas networks, and the production of 
green methanol and green ammonia, alongside carbon-capture-and-utilization initiatives at our thermal stations.A foray into nuclear power through ASHVINI, our joint venture with NPCIL, advancing projects such as 2.8 
GW Mahi Banswara, in support of a substantial nuclear

Letter to the Shareholders 
Dear Shareholders,
The global energy landscape is changing rapidly. Geopolitical 
tensions, supply chain disruptions, commodity price volatility, climate commitments, and the expansion of digital infrastructure have made energy security a strategic priority for nations across the world. Energy security has never received this level of attention in history. Recent events have shown that economic growth, industrial competitiveness, and national resilience are closely linked to the availability of reliable and affordable energy.
For India, this has reinforced the need for a diversified and resilient 
energy ecosystem. The country’s installed power capacity has crossed 550 GW, with non-fossil sources accounting for more than 52% of the total. India has also achieved the milestone of 50% non-fossil installed capacity five years ahead of target, creating a strong foundation for sustainable growth.
India’s economic momentum remains robust, with GDP growth 
estimated at around 7.7%. Simultaneously, the country’s power demand is projected to grow by 6–6.5% annually over the coming years. Peak demand crossed 270 GW in FY26 and is projected by CEA to reach about 459 GW by FY36. Expansion in manufacturing, infrastructure, electric mobility, urbanisation, and digital services is expected to sustain this growth. In addition, the rapid expansion of AI, cloud computing, and data centres will increase the demand for reliable, high-quality, round-the-clock power.
In this environment, NTPC is well positioned to support India’s 
growth. Our installed capacity reached 89.1 GW in FY26, more than doubling over the last decade. During FY26, we achieved our highest-ever annual capacity addition of 9.62 GW, with nearly 60% of the additions coming from renewable energy sources. NTPC generated 432.2 billion units of electricity during the year, contributing 23.6% of India’s total power generation and reinforcing our role as a key pillar of the country’s energy system.
Our coal-based stations delivered a plant load factor of 72.04%, 
significantly above the national average, reflecting the efficiency and reliability of our operations. Our trading arm NTPC Vidyut Vyapar Nigam Limited traded 46.38 billion units of power during the year.
Strengthening domestic energy capabilities remains a key priority. 
NTPC Mining Limited has emerged as the third-largest coal mining company in India, with six operational mines and three under development. Captive coal production reached 48.65 million tonnes in FY26, which is nearly 18% of our annual requirement, helping improve fuel security and operational self-reliance.
We are also investing in the future of the utility sector. Artificial 
intelligence, predictive analytics, and advanced forecasting tools are being integrated across our generation, renewable, mining, and maintenance operations. These technologies will improve plant availability, optimise operations, reduce costs, and strengthen safety.
At the same time, we are expanding our capabilities in pumped 
storage projects and battery energy storage systems to support renewable integration and grid stability. We are also investing in next-generation energy storage technologies, including CO₂-based energy storage systems and vanadium redox flow batteries, to strengthen grid flexibility and long-duration storage capabilities. These technologies have the potential to complement conventional battery systems by providing longer discharge durations, improved operational flexibility. Our investments in these emerging storage solutions are aimed at building capabilities that will support future grid requirements and contribute to the development of a more resilient and reliable power system.
We have also entered the nuclear sector with the Mahi Banswara 
project in Rajasthan. In addition, studies are being undertaken across 34 sites in 13 States for future nuclear project development opportunities, and a site selection report for one location has been submitted to the Department of Atomic Energy for consideration.
Our thermal fleet will continue to play an important role in India’s 
energy mix. Through investments in emission control systems, flexible operations, biomass co-firing, water conservation, ash utilisation, and carbon management initiatives, we are making our thermal assets more efficient and environmentally responsible.
FY26 was also a strong year financially. We achieved our highest-
ever consolidated Profit After Tax of ₹27,546 crore, up 15% over the previous year, while standalone Profit After Tax increased 18% to ₹23,162 crore. Consolidated earnings per share stood at ₹27.90. We have maintained our record of consistent dividend payments for over three decades, with a dividend payout ratio of around 37.68% for FY26.
Looking ahead, NTPC’s growth will be guided by four priorities: 
meeting India’s rising electricity demand, strengthening energy security through domestic capabilities, expanding clean and flexible energy infrastructure, and leveraging digital technologies 
Gurdeep Singh
Chairman & Managing Director

Ensuring India's Energy Security 
Beyond GigaWatts (GWs)
Power generation remains the cornerstone of NTPC's business, 
underpinning India's economic growth and energy security. As 
the country's largest integrated power utility, NTPC has built a 
diversified generation portfolio spanning thermal, hydro, renewable, and nuclear energy, enabling it to reliably meet the nation's 
evolving electricity demand while advancing the clean energy 
transition. Guided by its Corporate Plan, the Company is pursuing balanced capacity expansion with a strong focus on operational 
excellence, fuel security, digitalisation, flexibility of conventional 
assets and accelerated deployment of low-carbon technologies. With an installed and under-construction portfolio aligned to the 
vision of achieving nearly 244 GW by 2037,  NTPC is strategically 
transforming from a conventional power producer into a diversified 
integrated energy company, ensuring affordable, reliable and 
sustainable power for India's long-term growth.Power Generation

BESS (GWh) 22 52NTPC continues to strengthen its position as India's largest 
integrated power utility by expanding and modernising its conventional generation portfolio. Thermal power remains the 
backbone of the country's energy system, providing reliable 
baseload electricity to support economic growth and facilitate large-scale renewable energy integration. The Company is 
enhancing operational efficiency through adoption of advanced 
technologies, digitalisation, flexible plant operations and life extension initiatives, while simultaneously reducing emissions 
through improved efficiency, biomass co-firing, flue gas 
desulphurisation systems and water conservation measures. These initiatives ensure that conventional generation continues to 
play a critical role in maintaining grid reliability while supporting 
India's transition towards a low-carbon energy future.Biomass co-firing is an integral component of NTPC's strategy to decarbonise conventional power generation while strengthening 
domestic fuel security. As the first utility in India to commercialise 
biomass co-firing at scale, NTPC has demonstrated the use of agro-residue-based biomass pellets as a partial substitute 
for coal, enabling the production of renewable energy through 
existing thermal power infrastructure. The initiative contributes to reducing greenhouse gas emissions, mitigating stubble burning, 
promoting sustainable agricultural residue management, and 
generating additional income opportunities for farmers and rural entrepreneurs. During FY 2025-26, the NTPC Group sourced 1.52 
million tonnes  of biomass, more than doubling the previous year's 
procurement, and expanded commercial biomass co-firing across multiple thermal power stations. The Company has awarded 
contracts for the supply of over 3 million tonnes of biomass 
pellets covering 22 stations , while also increasing the utilisation of 
municipal solid waste-derived torrefied charcoal as an alternative 
green fuel. These initiatives reinforce NTPC's commitment to 
cleaner thermal generation, circular economy principles and sustainable rural development.Conventional Biomass Co-firing

NTPC Group has played a pioneering role in advancing India's 
solar energy programme through the implementation of the National Solar Mission (NSM).  As the designated nodal agency 
for Phase-I of the Mission, NTPC, through NVVN, has facilitated the procurement and bundling of solar power with thermal power for supply to distribution utilities, thereby supporting large-scale

security and supporting the nation's decarbonisation objectives.

Waste to Energy
Waste-to-Energy (WtE) is an emerging pillar of NTPC Group's 
circular economy strategy, addressing the dual challenge of 
sustainable municipal solid waste (MSW) management and clean 
energy production. Through NTPC Vidyut Vyapar Nigam Limited (NVVN), the Group is developing indigenous MSW-to-Torrefied 
Charcoal projects that convert municipal waste into green 
charcoal for co-firing in thermal power plants, reducing landfill disposal, lowering greenhouse gas emissions and substituting 
imported coal. During FY 2025-26, the 600 TPD Varanasi Waste-
to-Charcoal Project  was commissioned, producing over 3,000 
tonnes of green charcoal,  which was supplied to NTPC Unchahar 
for co-firing. Building on this success, NTPC is implementing 
similar projects at Bhopal, Hubballi-Dharwad, Noida-Greater Noida, Gorakhpur and Meerut, while also extending project management 
support for upcoming facilities in Gurugram and Faridabad. These 
initiatives reinforce NTPC's commitment to the Swachh Bharat Mission, resource circularity and India's low-carbon transition.  Project Processing

Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) are a key pillar of 
NTPC Group's strategy to enable large-scale renewable energy 
integration, enhance grid flexibility and improve power system 
reliability. As India's energy transition accelerates, NTPC is developing a diversified portfolio of utility-scale BESS projects 
across co-located renewable energy installations and standalone 
applications. NTPC Group currently has a BESS portfolio of 38.9 
GWh which comprises 6.62 GWh under execution,  including 
5 GWh at thermal power stations under the regulated return framework. A further 1.8 GWh of BESS projects are under planning 
to strengthen our near-term storage portfolio. Beyond this, NTPC 
is developing a substantial Non-Solar Hour (NSH) BESS pipeline 
of 30.4 GWh  of which 18.6 GWh has already been tendered.
Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) form a cornerstone of NTPC Group's long-duration energy storage strategy, providing the 
flexibility required to integrate increasing shares of renewable energy while ensuring grid stability and energy security. The 
Group is developing a robust PSP portfolio across NTPC and its 
subsidiaries, positioning itself among India's leading developers of pumped hydro storage. As on 31 March 2026, the NTPC Group has 
a PSP portfolio of 18.0 GW , comprising 4.8 GW  under NTPC and 
13.2 GW  under THDC India Limited and NEEPCO. During the year, 
all four units of the 1,000 MW Tehri Pumped Storage Project were 
commissioned, marking a significant milestone in strengthening 
the Group's dispatchable clean energy portfolio. NTPC has also completed Preliminary Feasibility Reports (PFRs) for 21 PSPs,  
while Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) for multiple projects are under preparation, reinforcing the Group's strong project pipeline. Through continued investments in pumped storage infrastructure, Energy Storage

Fly ash is increasingly being recognized as a valuable resource that supports sustainable infrastructure development and circular 
economy objectives. NTPC has adopted a comprehensive 
approach towards ash management, focusing on maximizing productive utilization while minimizing environmental impact. 
Through its Ash Policy and proactive stakeholder engagement, 
the Company promotes the utilization of fly ash and bottom ash across a wide range of applications, including cement 
manufacturing, concrete production, ash bricks and blocks, road 
and embankment construction, mine void filling, land reclamation and other infrastructure projects. During FY 2025-26, NTPC 
Group generated approximately 100 million tonnes of ash and 
achieved an ash utilization level of 107% , including utilization of 
legacy ash, with 20 stations achieving 100% ash utilization. By 
transforming an industrial by-product into a valuable construction 
resource, NTPC is reducing the requirement for virgin raw materials, supporting sustainable infrastructure development 
and reinforcing its commitment to resource efficiency and 
environmental stewardship.
NTPC Group is promoting circular economy principles through 
the productive utilisation of Flue Gas Desulphurisation (FGD) 
gypsum generated from its thermal power stations. By facilitating 
the supply of FGD gypsum to cement and gypsum board manufacturers, the Group is reducing dependence on imported 
natural gypsum while creating value from industrial by-products. 
During FY 2025-26, approximately 9.12 lakh metric tonnes  of 
FGD gypsum were supplied to end-users from NTPC and Group 
power stations. This initiative supports resource efficiency, import 
substitution, sustainable industrial development and responsible environmental management, while generating an additional 
revenue stream from by-product utilisation. Circular Resource Management

business strategy.

energy transition commitment. The Company engages with a

Risk Management and Governance 
At NTPC, we view risk management as a strategic driver, integral 
to achieving our business objectives responsibly and sustainably. 
Given the diverse business models and operations across NTPC 
Limited and its JVs/Subsidiaries, it is essential for each entity to manage risks effectively. This entails establishing robust 
risk governance frameworks and structures, as well as the 
meticulous, timely identification, classification, and assessment of risks. Prioritizing risks based on their potential impact on the 
business and likelihood of occurrence is crucial, followed by the 
implementation of mitigation strategies. Additionally, fostering a strong risk culture, coupled with monitoring and reporting mechanisms, further enhances risk 
management practices. Moreover, our approach extends beyond 
conventional business risks to encompass environmental, social, and governance (ESG) related risks. This holistic perspective 
acknowledges the interconnectedness of risks across the entire 
organization, its stakeholders, and the value chain. 
Risk Governance
Risk management is integrated into our system of governance to provide effective oversight and support the consideration of risks 
when making key decisions or setting strategic goals. The Risk 
Management policy guides the company’s approach to managing risks. It covers the identification of internal and external risks 
specific to the organization, which includes operational, legal & 
compliance, strategic, technological, financial and environmental & social risks.
The internal audit team acts as a third line of defence and 
independently assure company's risk management practices. 
Notably, NTPC is among the first CPSEs to have its Enterprise 
Risk Management (ERM) policy audited by statutory auditors, underscoring its commitment to robust risk governance. Established in 2015, the Board-level Risk Management Committee 
(RMC) oversees Enterprise Risk Management for the Company, 
Chaired by the Director (Projects) and comprising of key directors and the Chief Risk Officer. The Committee ensures comprehensive 
coverage of the holistic risk environment across categories such 
as strategic, operational, financial, compliance, and emerging risks. The RMC actively facilitates the identification, assessment, 
prioritization, and mitigation of risks within these groups 
through timely action plans. This structured approach enhances organizational resilience, drives informed decision-making, and 
contributes to long-term value creation for stakeholders.
The Chief Risk Officer (CRO) at NTPC holds a critical role in 
overseeing the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) process and reporting its compliance to the Board of Directors. The key 
responsibilities include designing, reviewing, and continuously 
enhancing ERM processes; preparing comprehensive enterprise-wide risk reports for the Risk Management Committee and the 
Board; and regularly updating them on the ERM status and key 
risks with actionable insights. The CRO also ensures effective implementation and validation of the ERM Policy across all 
functions, assists in developing and refining ERM policies to strengthen the company’s resilience, and promotes a strong 
ERM culture through awareness and capacity-building initiatives throughout the organization.
The Company’s risk management framework is aligned with the

Operational Risks 
These risks are critical for NTPC as they directly 
impact plant availability, reliability, employee safety, 
and uninterrupted power generation. It includes safety 
and hazard-related incidents, operational disruptions, equipment failures, and fuel security challenges that may 
affect generation capacity and efficiency. Our approach 
focuses on strengthening safety systems, preventive maintenance, emergency preparedness, and robust fuel 
planning. We also emphasize continuous monitoring, 
process controls, and operational excellence to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient operations.
Strategic Risks 
Strategic risks can influence NTPC’s long-term growth, competitiveness, and ability to respond to changes in 
the power sector. These risks include policy shifts in 
power procurement, changing market dynamics, energy transition-related developments, and the financial health 
of DISCOMs, which may impact demand, revenue 
realization, and future investment decisions. NTPC’s mitigation approach includes strategic planning, 
diversification of its generation portfolio, stakeholder 
engagement, and continuous monitoring of sectoral and policy developments. Technological Risks 
These risks are becoming increasingly relevant as NTPC 
adopts digital systems, automation, and technology-driven operational processes. These risks include 
cybersecurity threats, data breaches, system failures, 
and business continuity challenges that may affect critical operations and information assets. Our mitigation 
approach includes strengthening cybersecurity 
controls, enhancing IT governance, conducting periodic assessments, and maintaining business continuity 
and disaster recovery plans. We are also focused on 
improving digital resilience to support secure, reliable, and uninterrupted operations.Legal and Compliance Risks Given the power sector's highly regulated nature and the evolving legal, environmental, and governance landscape, 
effective compliance management is essential. These 
risks may arise from changes in laws, regulatory requirements, contractual obligations, statutory 
approvals, litigation, and non-compliance with applicable 
standards. NTPC aims to mitigate these risks through strong compliance monitoring, legal review mechanisms, 
internal controls, and regular engagement with regulatory 
authorities. 
Environmental and Social Risks Environmental and social risks are increasingly important due to the growing impact of climate change, 
resource constraints, stakeholder expectations, and 
sustainability-related regulations. These risks include physical and transition risks from climate change, 
water security, chemical safety, talent attraction 
and retention, occupational health and safety, and community development-related concerns. NTPC’s 
approach focuses on climate resilience, responsible 
resource use, environmental safeguards, safe handling of chemicals, workforce capability building, and 
inclusive community engagement. We aim to integrate 
ESG considerations into decision-making to support sustainable and responsible growth.Financial Risks 
Finance risks can affect our profitability, liquidity, 
capital allocation, and overall financial stability. These risks may arise from interest rate movements, 
foreign exchange fluctuations, fuel cost variations, 
counterparty credit risks, delayed receivables, and changes in financing conditions. NTPC seeks 
to manage these risks through prudent financial 
planning, robust internal controls, effective treasury management, and regular monitoring of financial 
exposures. The Company’s approach is aimed at 
maintaining financial resilience, supporting business continuity, and enabling sustainable value creation. 
Business Continuity Plan (BCP)
In line with our commitment to operational resilience, we have established comprehensive Business Continuity Plans (BCP). As 
a power generation Company, we recognize that adverse events 
may disrupt critical business operations, including generation, transmission, and related services. In such circumstances, 
our priority is to safeguard employees, associates, and other 
stakeholders, while continuing essential services at predefined acceptable levels.
Our Business Continuity Plan (BCP) is supported by the Enterprise 
Risk Management framework, which helps identify, assess, 
and mitigate internal and external risks that may affect critical 
operations. Business Impact Analysis is carried out to identify activities essential for business continuity and to prioritize resources accordingly. BCPs are developed for business units in alignment with the National Disaster Management Authority 
guidelines, NTPC’s Emergency Response Planning guidance, and 
the Company’s Cyber Security Policy.
We focus on adequate resource planning, compliance with 
applicable laws and statutory requirements, and proactive strengthening of internal systems and capabilities. The 
effectiveness of our business continuity approach is supported 
through communication, training of key stakeholders, mock drills, internal audits, and continuous learning. This enables us 
to improve preparedness and respond effectively to operational 
disruptions.

Simplification of Vigilance Clearance process 
The vigilance clearance process has been streamlined through 
the introduction of an online matrix-based decision system. This 
matrix outlines specific parameters for granting or withholding vigilance clearance, replacing the previous approach where only 
approved vigilance status was shared with the Human Resources 
department for manual interpretation and assessment.
Capacity Building  
Master trainers have been developed in specialized areas, 
including Investigation and Report Writing, Framing of Charge-sheets, and Conducting Competency Test Examinations. Through 
targeted vigilance programs and dedicated courses, approximately 
16,068 employees received training during the reporting period, significantly enhancing the organization's vigilance capabilities 
and awareness.
Annual Vigilance Executive Meeting
The Annual Vigilance Executive Meeting was organized to strengthen preventive vigilance practices, enhance capacity 
building capabilities, sensitize vigilance executives on emerging 
issues related to Artificial Intelligence adoption and data protection, and promote knowledge-sharing of best practices across NTPC. In 
addition, quarterly meetings were held at Ratnagiri and PMI-Noida 
facilities to discuss guideline changes and case management updates.
Publications and Awareness Materials
The second edition of "Satark Urja" was released during Vigilance Awareness Week 2025, highlighting the expanded scope of outreach 
and activities undertaken during the awareness campaign. Additionally, various NTPC business units published unit-specific vigilance magazines to promote decentralized vigilance awareness and broader stakeholder engagement.Strengthening Preventive Vigilance through  System-Driven Task Allocation  
Enhancements to the Complaint Handling Module enable the Chief Vigilance Officer and relevant supervisory officers to assign targeted scrutiny activities, inspections, and compliance checks 
to Site Vigilance Officers based on complaint analysis. The 
system provides end-to-end digital workflow coverage including task assignments, processing, approval, and completion tracking, 
thereby enhancing accountability, traceability, and the timeliness 
of preventive interventions. SOPs, Preventive Vigilance Measures, and System Strengthening 
Comprehensive Standard Operating Procedures have been issued and implemented across the following areas:Management Audit of Vigilance Unit (MAVU) by CVC  
NTPC underwent its inaugural Management Audit of Vigilance Unit by the Central Vigilance Commission. Based on the audit 
observations discussed with the Chief Vigilance Officer, the Alleged Employee Entry Module was developed and rolled out to 
further strengthen the online vigilance clearance system.
Quarterly Awareness Program 2025 
As part of this initiative, one designated week in each quarter 
focuses on raising awareness regarding key areas commonly associated with compliance violations. During the April–June 
2025 quarter, the first week of May was dedicated to "Provident 
Fund and Labour Compliance Matters." Awareness was disseminated through talks, informative banners and displays, 
vendor engagement sessions, and educational pamphlets.
Alleged Employee Entry Module
The online module is also introduced to ensure capture of employee details at the stage of complaint registration itself, in line with CVC 
observations during MAVU audit, thereby strengthening vigilance 
clearance integrity and traceability. 
Ministry of Power Vigilance Online Reporting System  
(MoP-ORS)  
In response to Ministry of Power requirements, NTPC developed the Ministry of Power Online Reporting System as a centralized digital platform for standardized, secure, and time-bound 
submission of monthly and quarterly reports by all Central Public 
Sector Undertakings (CPSUs) and departments. The system has replaced earlier manual and semi-manual processes involving 
postal and email-based submissions.Vigilance Clearance Processes for Joint Venture and Subsidiary

and processing timelines. This eliminates redundant cross-
functional communications and improves processing efficiency and consistency.Scrutiny of Annual Property Returns and Medical Claims: Formulated to ensure standardized, transparent, and systematic review mechanisms across NTPC and its subsidiaries and joint 
ventures.

Financial Capital 
Financial Capital serves as the strategic engine to drive 
the generation, deployment and optimization of all social, 
environmental, and governance initiatives within the NTPC Limited. 
By effectively leveraging our robust base of equity, reserves, and diversified debt portfolios backed by consistent operational 
cash flows, the Company maintains the agility to sustain and 
grow extensive nationwide operations. Our strong credit profile, reflected in the highest ratings from CRISIL, ICRA, India Ratings, 
and CARE, along with foreign ratings from Fitch, S&P , and Moody’s 
at par with sovereign ratings, enables us to efficiently access both domestic and international borrowing markets.
At NTPC, we actively align our financing approach with our 
business strategy of operational efficiency and diversification, 
while continuing to invest in backward and forward integration 
across the energy sector value chain. Our focus remains on financial stewardship to facilitate breakthrough investments in 
energy security, optimization, and transition, ensuring maximum 
value for our stakeholders through a resilient and high-performing balance sheet.Sustainability is embedded at the core of NTPC’s financial approach, shaping capex planning, project evaluation, and risk management. Financial investments are carried out to improve the efficiency and reliability of existing assets, expand non-fossil capacity, and build enabling infrastructure such as grid-scale storage, digital capabilities, and water-efficient systems. Our financial planning accounts for 
climate-related actions and market shifts to strengthen resilience, i.e., diversifying revenue streams, maintaining prudent leverage, and 
ensuring access to long-tenor funding.

Management of Financial Capital
NTPC’s capital allocation is guided by a structured decision 
framework prioritizing system reliability, sustainability, and long-
term value creation. Investment decisions are evaluated through 
financial and non-financial lenses, including expected returns across the asset life, project risks, execution readiness, regulatory alignment, and contribution to transition objectives. We prioritize 
projects that strengthen reliability, flexibility, and efficiency while 
enabling a higher share of renewables in the grid.In a regulated and largely contract-backed power sector, cash 
realization and receivables management are central to financial 
resilience. NTPC sustains liquidity through disciplined billing and collection processes supported by sector payment security mechanisms, continuous engagement with counterparties, and 
strong internal controls. This helps protect cash flow, reduce 
short-term borrowing dependence, and improve the predictability of capital deployment.
NTPC maintains a disciplined approach to capital management to support long-term investments and operational efficiency requirements. Funding strategies are aligned with asset lifecycles, 
with a focus on maintaining a balanced capital structure, diversified borrowing sources and adequate liquidity. Active 
treasury management helps monitor refinancing, interest-rate and liquidity risks while preserving financial flexibility and funding 
readiness for future growth opportunities.Disciplined working capital management supports NTPC is able to sustain its capital investment programme efficiently while 
maintaining financial flexibility. By aligning cash flows with project requirements and operational priorities, NTPC is able to sustain 
investment momentum across generation, renewable energy and 
infrastructure projects without compromising financial stability. 
The composition of capital expenditure demonstrates NTPC's balanced approach to growth and transition. Alongside investments in renewable energy, NTPC deployed ₹4,284.91 crore towards hydro 
projects and ₹3,243.36 crore towards emission-control initiatives, 
strengthening environmental performance and regulatory preparedness. Investments in green hydrogen, battery energy storage systems and other emerging technologies further support the development of future growth platforms and enhance long-term 
business resilience.NTPC's capital deployment is focused on strengthening India's 
energy security while advancing the development of a cleaner 
and more diversified energy portfolio. At NTPC, we continuously 
invest in high-efficiency thermal capacity and environmental technological upgrades to ensure reliability, while scaling our 
renewable energy, pumped storage, and green hydrogen portfolios. 
Our capital allocation is governed by a disciplined framework prioritizing execution of readiness, lifecycle returns, and long-term 
regulatory alignment. During FY 2025–26, NTPC invested ₹49,067.87 crore towards 
capacity expansion, sustainability initiatives and operational 
resilience. Investments in non-fossil and transition-related assets 
amounted to ₹25,127.52 crore, representing 51% of total capital expenditure, up from 24% in the previous year, reflecting our 
continued focus on building a diversified energy portfolio and 
supporting India's long-term energy security and decarbonization ambitions. Renewable energy remained the largest area of 
investment, with capital expenditure of ₹16,699.95 crore, 
complemented by investments in hydro projects, environmental infrastructure, nuclear capacity, and emerging technologies.Capital allocation frameworkWorking capital discipline and collections

Manufactured capital remains fundamental to NTPC’s ability to 
deliver reliable, affordable and sustainable electricity on a scale. 
As India’s one of the largest integrated power utilities, NTPC 
operates a large and diversified portfolio of generation assets that ensure stable baseload supply, while supporting grid resilience in 
an evolving energy landscape. 
The Company continues to strengthen its asset base through 
capacity addition, modernization of existing assets, and 
technology upgradation. While thermal generation continues to provide system stability, NTPC is progressively transitioning 
towards a diversified energy mix with a significant increase in 
renewable capacity, energy storage, and green hydrogen solutions.
This balanced approach enables NTPC to maintain reliability of 
supply while aligning its manufactured capital with long-term decarbonisation and sustainability objectives.NTPC follows a structured and integrated asset management framework built on the principles of reliability, lifecycle efficiency, 
and responsible resource stewardship. The framework spans 
project planning, execution, operations, modernisation, and end-of-life decisions, with policies and systems designed to optimise 
performance while minimising environmental impact. 
The Corporate Plan 2037 sets the direction for capacity expansion 
and diversification, while engineering, procurement and project 
management standards govern the planning, design, construction and commissioning of generating assets. Our Operations and 
Maintenance framework brings together standardised practices, 
condition-based monitoring, predictive maintenance and reliability-centred approaches to ensure consistent plant performance. Performance is tracked through centralised monitoring systems, real-time analytics and benchmarking against industry standards. 
Integrated management systems aligned with global standards 
on quality, environment, and occupational health and safety provide the structure for continual improvement. Sustainability 
is embedded across the asset lifecycle through deployment 
of supercritical and ultra-supercritical technologies, flue gas desulphurisation systems, biomass co-firing, water and ash 
management practices, and a steadily expanding renewable 
portfolio. Digital transformation, including remote monitoring centres, AI/ML-based diagnostics, drone-based inspections, and 
ERP-enabled workflows, is increasingly woven into day-to-day 
operations.
NTPC operates across an integrated value chain that spans generation, mining, fuel management, transmission support, renewables, hydro, nuclear, green hydrogen, e-mobility, ash 
utilisation, consultancy and power trading. The performance of these verticals during the year, taken together, reflects steady 
progress on capacity addition, operational reliability and energy transition initiatives.

Gas-based generation remains an important component of 
NTPC's diversified generation portfolio, providing operational 
flexibility and supporting grid stability. In response to the 
reduced availability of domestic gas supplies, the Company adopted a flexible fuel sourcing strategy through long-term RLNG 
arrangements, spot market procurement, and gas exchange 
platforms. NTPC continued to optimize fuel procurement through a mix of contracted and market-based sourcing while maintaining adequate liquid fuel reserves to support operational requirements. 
During FY 2025-26, gas consumption, including that of RGPPL, 
stood at approximately 805 MMSCM , reflecting the prevailing fuel 
availability and dispatch requirements. These measures enabled 
NTPC to ensure reliable operation of its gas-based assets while 
adapting to evolving market conditions.NTPC continued to strengthen its renewable energy asset base during FY 2025-26, reinforcing its position as one of 
India's leading clean energy developers. As on 31 March 
2026, the Company's commissioned renewable energy portfolio reached 11,547 MW,  comprising 10,654 MW 
of solar capacity  and 893 MW of wind capacity.  This 
growing portfolio reflects NTPC's sustained investments in utility-scale renewable infrastructure across the country.  
  
In addition to its operational portfolio, NTPC had 15,040 MW 
of renewable capacity under execution  as of 31 March 2026, 
including 9,403 MW of solar projects  and 5,637 MW of wind projects. The sizeable under-construction portfolio demonstrates 
the Company's strong project development capabilities 
and provides a solid foundation for future capacity growth.  
  
Through continued development of solar parks, wind projects, hybrid renewable solutions, transmission-linked infrastructure, 
and emerging energy assets, NTPC is expanding its clean energy infrastructure while enhancing the resilience and sustainability 
of its generation portfolio. This strategic build-out of renewable 
assets supports the Company's long-term objective of diversifying its generation mix and creating enduring value 
through low-carbon energy infrastructure.Biomass co-firing is an important component of NTPC's strategy 
to decarbonise thermal power generation while enhancing fuel diversification and supporting rural livelihoods. As a pioneer 
in commercial-scale biomass co-firing in India, NTPC has 
successfully integrated agro residue-based biomass pellets into its coal-fired power plants, enabling partial substitution of coal 
with a carbon-neutral fuel. This initiative contributes to reducing 
greenhouse gas emissions, mitigating crop residue burning and creating additional income opportunities for farmers and biomass 
aggregators. Building on the successful demonstration at Dadri, 
NTPC has expanded biomass co-firing across multiple stations and continues to strengthen its biomass supply ecosystem 
through long-term procurement arrangements and supplier 
partnerships. These efforts support cleaner thermal generation while advancing the Company's commitment to sustainable and inclusive energy transition.
After successfully demonstrating biomass co-firing at Dadri plant, NTPC has started commercial scale biomass co-firing at other NTPC stations also. In total NTPC has awarded 10.18 Million MT of Biomass pellets for 22 stations including 04 JVs (APCPL-Jhajjar, Meja, 
NSPCL Bhilai & Rourkela). The total receipt of Biomass pellets upto 31st March 2026 is 3.105 Lakh MT. Gas Consumption Renewable Energy Generation

Water is both a critical input for our operations and a shared 
resource with the communities around us. As part of our CEO 
Water Mandate commitments, we continue to strengthen 
water stewardship through responsible operational practices, engagement with local communities, collaboration with 
stakeholders, transparent disclosure of performance, and 
initiatives aimed at improving long-term water resilience across the regions in which we operate. Our Water Policy and Rainwater 
Harvesting Policy set the framework, and our implementation 
strategy is built on the Reduce–Reuse–Recycle approach.
We are systematically deploying water conservation technologies across our thermal fleet to reduce 
freshwater dependency and build resilience in water-stressed regions.Nearly all thermal stations operate with closed-cycle cooling systems and cooling towers. We are also expanding the use of treated wastewater, increasing cycles of concentration, 
strengthening rainwater harvesting infrastructure, and 
implementing advanced recycling systems to optimise water use across our operations. Water Stewardship

We prioritize waste reduction at source through process optimization, efficient resource utilization, and adoption of digital initiatives. 
The continued implementation of Project PRADIP has significantly reduced paper consumption while enhancing operational efficiency, 
transparency, and decision-making processes.
As part of our business operations and maintenance, hazardous 
waste such as used lubricating oil, transformer oil, spent resins, used containers, and other process residues are generated and 
these wastes are managed in strict compliance with the Hazardous 
and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016, and subsequent amendments. 
E-waste and waste batteries generated from plant operations 
are managed in accordance with the E-Waste (Management) 
Rules 2022 and the Battery Waste Management Rules 2022, and subsequent amendments. These wastes are disposed of through 
buyback arrangements with manufacturers or suppliers and through authorized recyclers and dismantlers to ensure environmentally 
sound recycling and resource recovery.
Municipal solid waste generated across townships and operational 
units is managed through composting, bio-methanation,

Ash, a by-product of coal-fired thermal power plants, has now 
gained recognition as a valuable resource material worldwide, 
suitable for diverse applications in the field of Civil Engineering. 
Extensive endeavors are being undertaken at various levels to 
effectively utilize ash in different applications, leading to significant achievements in ash utilization.
The latest Gazette Notification of the Ministry of Environment, 
Forests & Climate Change (MoEF&CC), Government of India, 
introduces guidelines for thermal power plants (TPPs) and ash 
user agencies regarding the utilization of both generated ash and legacy ash. In line with the notification, NTPC places significant 
emphasis on sustainable ash utilization as a key focus area within 
its operations. The Company is committed to maximizing the utilization of ash across all its power plants. 
During the Financial Year 2025-26, approximately ~100 million 
tons of ash was generated by NTPC Group stations and 107% 
i.e., ~107 million tons of ash had been gainfully utilized in various 
areas such as issue to industries for cement, concrete, bricks/ blocks making, road embankment construction, mine filling, land 
development works etc. Twenty stations have achieved 100% ash 
utilization.Ash Management 
Reducing air emissions remains one of NTPC's key environmental priorities. The Company employs a combination of advanced pollution 
control technologies, real-time monitoring systems, and large-scale environmental infrastructure investments to manage emissions from thermal operations.
Our investments span Flue Gas Desulphurization (FGD) systems for SOx control, combustion modifications and Low NOx burners for 
NOx reduction, and upgraded Electrostatic Precipitators (ESPs) for Particulate Matter (PM) control. 
Electrostatic Precipitators (ESP):  To control particulate matter emissions, NTPC has deployed highly efficient Electrostatic 
Precipitators (ESPs) across its thermal fleet, achieving removal efficiencies of over 99.8%. Renovation & Modernization (R&M) 
of ESPs has been undertaken wherever required. 
Flue Gas Desulphurization (FGD): 55 units of Flue Gas Desulphurization (FGD) systems are commissioned with a total capacity 
of 30,250 megawatts and 90 units of FGD installation is in progress across NTPC plants.
NOx Reduction:  NTPC has implemented combustion modifications and De-NOx measures across its thermal fleet to meet 
regulatory emission requirements. Modifications have been completed in all 50 identified units, enabling reduction of nitrogen 
oxide (NOx) emissions to prescribed limits.
CEMS and CAAQMS:  Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (CEMS) and Continuous  Ambient Air Quality Monitoring 
Systems are operational across the fleet, enabling continuous monitoring and regulatory reporting. The real-time monitoring 
data is transmitted to relevant regulatory authorities.
Other Air Emissions Management:  NTPC continues to monitor ozone-depleting substances (ODS) and other priority pollutants 
as part of its environmental management framework. Mercury emissions are maintained below the minimum detectable 
limit (MDL), and the Company has completely phased out the use of Polychlorinated Biphenyls (PCBs) across its operations, 
reinforcing its commitment to responsible environmental stewardship.Air (Non-GHG) Emission Management

We track Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions 
on a Group basis, with specific CO₂ emission intensity (tCO₂ per 
MWh) as the primary decarbonisation progress metric. With our non-fossil capacity increased by 51.95% in FY 2025-26, and the 
continued ramp-up of renewable generation, we expect emission 
intensity to trend downward as the portfolio mix evolves. At NTPC, we are committed to supporting India's Panchamrit goals 
achieving net zero emissions by 2070, reaching 500 GW of non-fossil 
capacity by 2030, and reducing emissions intensity of GDP by 45% 
by 2030. The Company is pursuing a diversified energy transition strategy encompassing renewable energy, green hydrogen, energy storage, carbon capture and utilisation, biomass co-firing, nuclear 
energy, and nature-based carbon sinks.
In collaboration with NITI Aayog, we are co-developing a comprehensive Net Zero GHG Emissions Roadmap, aligning with 
India's Panchamrit targets while balancing energy security and affordability. Separately, NTPC has entered a strategic partnership with Sustainable Energy for All (SEforALL) to formulate an energy 
transition roadmap. NTPC is among the first global energy companies 
to declare an Energy Compact at the UN High-Level Dialogue on Energy, committing to measurable SDG7-aligned outcomes. 
NVVN, NTPC's wholly owned subsidiary, leads the Group's carbon management strategy through a centralised approach 
to carbon portfolio development, project registration, carbon 
market participation, and stakeholder engagement. The Carbon Management Group works to identify and advance carbon mitigation 
opportunities across NTPC and its subsidiaries while supporting the 
Group's broader decarbonisation and energy transition objectives. Its activities span project registration, verification and issuance, carbon 
trading, capacity building, policy engagement, and participation in 
emerging domestic and international carbon markets.As part of this strategy, NTPC is progressively building a diversified carbon portfolio across renewable energy, hydro, waste-to-energy, 
afforestation, and other low-carbon initiatives. Projects are being 
registered under internationally recognised carbon programmes, including the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM), Verified Carbon 
Standard (VCS), Global Carbon Council (GCC), and International 
Carbon Registry (ICR), enabling the Group to generate verified emission reductions while supporting India's low-carbon transition

Human Capital 
Human capital stands central to NTPC's ability to deliver reliable, 
sustainable power today while simultaneously building capabilities 
for an evolving energy portfolio. As India progresses toward its 
clean energy and Net Zero aspirations, NTPC recognizes that its human capital is an asset for its business growth and resilience. 
The people strategy for FY 2025–26 centers on strengthening 
workforce and performance management, creating a continuous learning culture through structured capability building, embedding 
Diversity, Equity and Inclusion across the organization, enabling 
comprehensive wellbeing and work-life balance, and reinforcing human rights and labour practices alongside occupational 
health and safety across all employees and contract workforce. 
This integrated approach ensures that NTPC builds not only the operational excellence required today but also develops the future-
ready capabilities essential for India's energy transition toward a 
Viksit Bharat.
NTPC is committed to drive a workplace that is inclusive, diverse, and equitable for all employees and workers, irrespective of their backgrounds. During FY 2025–26, the Company strengthened its 
commitment through the introduction of a dedicated Diversity, 
Equity and Inclusion (DEI) Policy, reinforcing its aim to drive fair, transparent, inclusive, and equal opportunities for all employees 
and workers across its employment lifecycle. The policy reflects 
NTPC's longstanding principle of equal opportunity and equal remuneration, underscoring discrimination based on gender, 
caste, religion, nationality, sexual orientation, economic status, or 
political opinions has no place within the Company.
During FY 2025–26, the gender mix for NTPC's workforce 
comprised 92.17% male employees and 7.83% female employees. Female workforce representation stood at 2%, with 37 women in 
senior management positions, reflecting Company’s continuous 
engagement and efforts towards enhancing gender diversity across the Company.Overview

NTPC successfully implemented the Prime Minister Internship

towards nation-building through youth empowerment,

Affairs (MCA) as part of the Government of India’s initiative 
to provide large-scale internship opportunities to youth in top companies, aims to bridge the gap between academic learning 
and real-life workplace exposure. In alignment with the objectives 
and operational framework prescribed under the PMIS Guidelines, NTPC adopted a transparent, technology-enabled and welfare-
oriented implementation model focused on quality learning 
outcomes and inclusive participation.
During FY 2025–26, NTPC demonstrated strong institutional 
commitment towards the Scheme by creating internship opportunities beyond the indicative annual capacity communicated 
under PMIS. Across Pilot Rounds 1 and 2, the Company created 
more than 6,900 internship opportunities and ensured issuance of internship offers to 100% of eligible candidates available through 
the MCA portal, subject to prescribed screening guidelines 
and organizational eligibility requirements. NTPC received an encouraging response from aspiring candidates across the 
country, with over 15,000 applications received across the two 
rounds, reflecting the credibility and attractiveness of the Company as a preferred learning destination for youth.
The Company established robust systems for transparent 
offer issuance, centralized monitoring and process-driven 
implementation in line with the Government’s emphasis on 
accountability and measurable outcomes. Timely stipend disbursal was ensured through streamlined attendance 
management and centralized follow-up mechanisms. NTPC also 
maintained an efficient grievance redressal framework, ensuring disposal or escalation of grievances within stipulated timelines, 
thereby supporting the Scheme’s objective of responsive and 
participant-centric governance.
NTPC adopted a holistic approach towards intern welfare and 
experiential learning. Interns were provided additional support facilities including snacks and lunch arrangements/subsidized 
canteen access, joining kits, safety kits, access to medical 
facilities wherever available, and additional Personal Accident Insurance coverage of ₹5 lakh over and above the Government-
provided insurance support. From Pilot Round 3 onwards, interns 
are also being provided attendance-linked financial support towards snacks and lunch. These initiatives reinforced NTPC’s 
commitment towards creating a safe, inclusive and enabling learning environment aligned with the broader social objectives 
of the Scheme.
The Company placed strong emphasis on structured capability 
development and workplace readiness. NTPC achieved 100% 
mentor mapping for interns and conducted structured classroom 
training programmes covering safety practices, technical skills, personality development, communication and other 
employability-oriented soft skills. Certification programmes in MS 
Office and exposure to advanced AR/VR learning modules further strengthened experiential learning outcomes and digital readiness 
of interns. Progress of interns was periodically monitored on 
parameters such as technical ability, punctuality, teamwork, flexibility and communication skills, ensuring continuous 
assessment and guided development throughout the internship 
period.
NTPC further strengthened the outreach and inclusiveness of 
PMIS during the year by expanding participation to additional stations, Regional Headquarters, Joint Ventures and subsidiaries 
under Pilot Round 3. This expansion enabled wider geographical 
coverage and diversified learning opportunities for participating youth while supporting the Government’s vision of large-scale 
industry participation under the Scheme.

Occupational health and safety (OHS) remains a core pillar of 
NTPC's human capital strategy, reflecting the belief that no 
business objective or production target justifies harm to people. 
NTPC has established a comprehensive Occupational Health and Safety Management System, aligned with the principles 
of ISO 45001:2018, covering employees, trainees, apprentices, 
consultants, contract workers and other personnel operating under the Company's control. NTPC seeks to strengthen workplace safety culture, safeguard worker wellbeing, and advance its aim of “zero incidents” across operations. 
The framework is built around four pillars: “Safety Policy and 
Objectives”, “Safety Risk Management”, “Safety Assurance” and 
“Safety Promotion” providing a structured approach to hazard 
identification, risk mitigation, operational control, workforce participation and continual improvement. 
NTPC's safety management approach extends beyond compliance 
and is embedded throughout the employee and contractor 
lifecycle. Workers are actively integrated into key safety processes including Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA), Job 
Safety Analysis (JSA), Permit-to-Work systems, incident reporting, 
emergency preparedness and safety assurance programmes. Regular safety inspections, audits, compliance assessments 
and management reviews support continuous monitoring and improvement of workplace safety performance across operating sites and project locations.
NTPC strengthened its occupational health and safety framework 
by adopting a digitally enabled solution, i.e., Contractor safety

Occupational health and safety training includes certification 
programmes from internationally recognized agencies including 
NEBOSH (National Examination Board in Occupational Safety 
and Health), IOSH (Institution of Occupational Safety and Health) 
and NOSA (National Occupational Safety Association), alongside 
programmes on behavioural safety, fire safety, electrical safety, incident investigation, height and rescue operations and safety leadership. These programmes build technical safety competence 
while simultaneously strengthening safety culture and individual 
safety consciousness.
To drive safety behaviour, toolbox talks are delivered at work sites; 
mass safety pep talks and mock drills conducted regularly, which enables reinforcement of safety messages, practices, and are 
embedded in daily work routines. For contractor workers, three 
critical modules Safety Induction, Fire Safety and Personal Protective Equipment usage are delivered directly by NTPC's Safety Department 
prior to gate pass issuance, establishing essential safety foundations 
before deployment.
Occupational health and safety remain an integral element of 
NTPC's human capital approach. Through structured safety training, workforce engagement, risk management processes, and 
regular performance monitoring, the Company seeks to strengthen 
workplace safety across its operations. The application of common safety standards, training requirements and safety controls to 
both employees and contractor personnel reflect NTPC's focus 
on protecting its workforce, supporting employee wellbeing and maintaining a safe and productive work environment.*Safety Incident data is at Consolidated level

NTPC upholds the principles of Human Rights to ensure its 
employees and workers live with social and economic dignity and 
freedom, irrespective of gender, caste, economic status, or religion. 
The Company’s Human Rights Policy aligns with internationally 
accepted standards including the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the Fundamental Conventions of the International 
Labour Organization. The Human Rights Policy explicitly covers 
gender equality and non-discrimination, supported by training and awareness programmes for employees and associates, including 
contractor personnel, to promote responsible workplace and 
community conduct.
Under the principal employer model, contractors are engaged for 
specific job roles, with primary responsibility for employee welfare resting with the contractor; however, NTPC ensures rigorous 
oversight of compliance, statutory, and internal requirements as 
part of its contract review mechanism. The key provisions include adherence to minimum and skill-based wages, payment through 
bank mode ensuring transparency and traceability, and coverage 
under provident fund, employees' state insurance and applicable social security schemes. Contractors must ensure that workers 
receive leaves or wages in lieu, maintaining continuity of financial 
security.
At the onboarding stage, contractors are required to ensure 
medical check-ups, insurance coverage and safety training for contract workers before deployment. Essential welfare facilities including canteens, medical support, drinking water, washrooms and rest areas are made available at plant and station locations, reflecting recognition that worker dignity extends beyond wages 
to encompass working conditions and basic facilities.
Compliance monitoring occurs through an HR No Objection 
Certificate System linked to contractor bill processing, with 
verification of wage payments and statutory challans prior to clearance. This systematic approach ensures that wages are 
paid correctly and on time, preventing worker exploitation. Timely 
wage payments are ensured even when contractors face delays, protecting worker financial security. Supply chain partners are 
expected to adhere to NTPC's human rights commitments, 
including applicable laws and regulations, extending responsible practices beyond direct employees to the broader value chain.
Worker engagement is facilitated through regular interaction with 
representatives via an institutionalized Communication Matrix, 
including structured meetings with unions and participative 
forums to discuss working conditions and labour rights. This approach ensures that workers have voice in matters affecting 
them and that management understands worker concerns and 
perspectives. Regular dialogue creates opportunities for early identification and resolution of issues before they escalate, 
demonstrating respect for worker agencies and Company’s 
commitment to fair practices.Human Rights and Labour Practices:

Intellectual Capital 
NTPC's intellectual capital comprises the intangible assets that 
enable consistent performance today and future-ready capability for 
tomorrow. It includes R&D capability through NETRA (NTPC Energy 
Technology Research Alliance), intellectual property, institutional knowledge, proprietary processes and digital systems, scientific 
services, data platforms, and cybersecurity practices. Together, 
these assets help NTPC anticipate and solve complex engineering and operating challenges, strengthen compliance and safety, and 
accelerate the energy transition through technology-led solutions.
NTPC recognises R&D as a cornerstone of technology leadership in 
the energy sector. The Company's R&D agenda prioritises applied solutions that strengthen reliability, safety and efficiency of existing 
assets, while also developing and validating transition-enabling 
technologies. Through NETRA, established in 2009 as our dedicated research hub, R&D is strategically aligned with India's energy 
transition priorities, including carbon capture, energy storage, green 
hydrogen, coal gasification, and waste-to-energy technologies. R&D continues to be embedded within NTPC's long-term strategic roadmap, with consistent allocation of over 2% of Profit Before 
Tax (PBT) towards R&D activities. The Company's priorities are guided by a high-level Research Advisory Council (RAC) comprising 
eminent scientists and global experts, and an in-house Scientific 
Advisory Council (SAC), strengthening plant performance, reliability, and cost reduction. The programme is aligned to the evolving needs 
of the Indian power system and focuses on CCUS, advanced energy 
storage, green hydrogen, coal gasification, ash utilization, and waste-to-energy technologies.First DV Kapur Foundation

Cybersecurity is governed as an enterprise risk priority and is 
reviewed through NTPC's risk governance structure, including Board-
level oversight via the Enterprise Risk Management framework. 
A dedicated cybersecurity operating model is led by the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), supported by a cross-functional 
cybersecurity cell with representation from IT, Operations Technology 
(OT), Finance, Legal, and Human Resources, ensuring holistic risk consideration and consistent implementation of security practices 
across corporate systems and critical operations. This structure enables clear accountability, faster incident coordination, and 
consistent implementation of security practices across corporate 
systems and critical operations.
To ensure round-the-clock vigilance, NTPC operates a 24×7 Security 
Operations Centre (SOC) for continuous monitoring and response. 
Employees are also sensitised to report suspicious activity to the SOC, strengthening early detection through both technology-led 
monitoring and human-led escalation.Cybersecurity Governance and 
Operating Model 
NTPC’s cybersecurity approach is anchored in its Cyber Security 
Policy, which is designed to protect information and systems through 
the core principles of Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA). 
The policy framework guides preventive and detective controls across the lifecycle of access, usage, monitoring, and response, and is aligned with applicable legal and regulatory expectations, including 
requirements related to data protection.NTPC strengthens cybersecurity assurance through a mix of internal reviews and independent assessments. The organization 
undertakes regular cybersecurity audits, Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT), and Operational technology security 
audits through CERT-In empaneled auditors across infrastructure, 
applications, networks, and operational environments. 
NTPC is in the process of implementing an Information Security Management System (ISMS) for its central Data Centre and is working towards 
ISO 27001 certification. This is being progressed as a formalisation and strengthening of existing policy-led controls and governance (i.e., 
“moving from controls in place” to “controls systematically governed, measured, and audited under an ISMS framework”).Approach to Cyber Security Cyber Assurance and Operational Resilience

Management
A Cyber Crisis Management Plan 
(CCMP) is in place to handle critical 
situations, outlining response structure, 
roles of the Cyber Crisis Management 
Committee, coordination with national 
agencies (CERT-In, NCIIPC), and both 
internal and external communication 
plans. On identification of an

isolating affected systems, blocking

guides corrective actions followed by 
restoration and statutory/intimation 
actions where required. Incidents are 
logged through ticketing systems, 
classified by severity, and handled 
within defined SLAs. NTPC maintains a Disaster 
Recovery Policy complementing its 
comprehensive Business Continuity 
Plan. A remote Disaster Recovery 
Data Centre stores backups of critical 
applications and data, configured for 
backup and quick failover to minimize 
downtime. Backup power systems 
including Uninterruptible Power 
Supplies (UPS) and diesel generators 
ensure continuous operation during 
power disruptions. Systems are 
configured with defined Recovery Time 
Objectives (RTOs) to restore critical 
systems within acceptable timeframes.

landscape and cybersecurity defenses. Critical software 
patches are applied in line with vendor recommendations 
and threat advisories. Cybersecurity infrastructure (firewalls, 
endpoint security solutions) is regularly updated to leverage 
improved features and address emerging threats. Non-
compliance with cybersecurity policy requirements is treated 
as a serious conduct issue subject to disciplinary action per 
HR rules.
